2019_129_011519org_regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education's organizational and regular meeting of January 15, 2019 at the Services Building. The organizational half elects the year's officers, appoints the assistant superintendent of business services as treasurer, establishes fund depositories and legal counsel, and sets the 2019 meeting schedule. The regular half is capital-work heavy: $968,348.03 of flooring replacement, $860,333.10 of roof replacement, $529,969.00 for the Troy High pool renovation, $152,065.00 of lockers at Boulan and Larson, and $30,827.94 of signage for the new Early Childhood Center.
2019_129_011519org_regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Organizational and regular meeting, January 15, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**The organizational half**
The first order of business is electing an acting chairperson to officiate until a president is elected, followed by the appointment of Judy Holmes as temporary secretary. The Board then elects a president, vice president and secretary in turn, each nomination requiring a second and a motion to close nominations — the agenda memo from Dr. Machesky notes that **four votes are required for election**. The treasurer is appointed annually as a nonvoting officer; by board policy the assistant superintendent of business services has served in that role and the superintendent recommends the practice continue. The remaining organizational items establish fund depositories and the investment resolution for 2018/19 and 2019/20, designate board and district legal counsel, designate the superintendent as deputy secretary, designate a person for posting notices of meetings, and adopt the meeting schedule for the 2019 calendar year.

**Recognition**
A Mission Moment on the Baker Middle School food drive, and Board Recognition Month.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the December 4, 2018 workshop and the December 18, 2018 meeting, the November 2018 Treasurer's Report, and Budget Adjustment #1 — a 2018-19 budget amendment resolution restating total revenues and unappropriated fund balance estimated to be available.

**Business — five capital awards**

| Project | Award | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flooring replacement | $968,348.03 | Building Site and Sinking Fund |
| Roof replacement | $860,333.10 | 2016 Capital Projects Fund |
| Troy High pool renovation | $529,969.00 | 2016 Capital Projects and Sinking Fund |
| Boulan and Larson lockers | $152,065.00 | — |
| Early Childhood Center signage | $30,827.94 | — |

The flooring award splits between Conventional Carpet, Inc. at $829,598.03 and Kuhn Specialty Flooring at $112,500.00, with $15,000.00 set aside for additional and emergency flooring and $11,250.00 of contingency. The roofing award covers elementary schools, Smith Middle School and the Operations Building, with Quality Roofing taking Athens High School at $197,421.00 and $78,212.10 held as contingency. The pool renovation divides among B & B Pools for pool upgrades at $209,090.00, Shoreview Electric at $123,400.00 and Paint Plus for painting at $149,300.00, with $48,179.00 of contingency. Signage for the Early Childhood Center goes to ASI Sign at $30,827.94.

**Other**
The Board adopts its 2019 committee assignments and takes a first reading of revisions to board policies.
2019_129_011519org_regmtg.verbose:
Agenda packet for the organizational and regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, January 15, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Election of Acting Chairperson; 3. Appointment of Temporary Secretary; 4. Annual Organizational Meeting of the Board of Education — A. Nomination and Election of Officers (President, Vice President, Secretary), B. Appointment of Treasurer, C. Establish Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution for 2018/19 and 2019/20, D. Designation of Board and District Legal Counsel, E. Designation of Superintendent to be Deputy Secretary, F. Designation of a Person for Posting Notices of Meetings, G. Meeting Schedule for 2019 Calendar Year; 5. Recognition — A. Mission Moment: Baker Middle School Food Drive, B. Board Recognition Month; 6. Additions & Deletions; 7. Public Communication (agenda items); 8. General – Consent Agenda; 9. Personnel; 10. Curriculum; 11. Business; 12. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 13. Other; 14. Adjournment.

**The agenda memo.** Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D. writes to the Board setting out the organizational sequence. The first order of business is to elect an acting chairperson who will conduct the meeting until a president has been elected. Each officer election follows the same procedure: the chair declares nominations in order, a nomination is made and seconded, and a motion and support are made to close nominations; the memo states plainly that four votes are required for election. After the president is elected, the newly elected president declares nominations in order for vice president, then for secretary, following the same procedures. On the treasurer, the memo records that by Board Policy the treasurer is appointed annually by the Board as a nonvoting officer, that the assistant superintendent of business services has served as treasurer of the Board, and that the superintendent recommends this procedure continue.

**Organizational items.** Item 2 resolves that a named member serve as acting chairperson to officiate the meeting until the election of a president has been completed. Item 3 suggests the acting chairperson appoint Judy Holmes to act as temporary secretary until the secretary of the Troy Board of Education has been elected. Item 4.A.1 provides the nomination form for president — one member nominating another to serve as president of the Troy Board of Education until December 31, 2019 — followed by the close of nominations and a suggested resolution, with the same structure repeated for vice president and secretary. Item 4.B appoints the treasurer. Item 4.C establishes fund depositories and the investment resolution for both 2018/19 and 2019/20. Item 4.D designates board and district legal counsel; 4.E designates the superintendent to be deputy secretary of the Board; 4.F designates a person responsible for posting notices of meetings; and 4.G adopts the meeting schedule for the 2019 calendar year.

**Recognition.** Item 5.A is a Mission Moment on the Baker Middle School food drive; item 5.B recognizes Board Recognition Month.

**Consent agenda.** A. Minutes of the December 4, 2018 Board of Education Workshop; B. Minutes of the December 18, 2018 Board of Education Meeting; C. Treasurer's Report for November 2018; D. Budget Adjustment #1. The budget item is a 2018-19 Budget Amendment Resolution which resolves that the total revenues and unappropriated fund balance estimated to be available are as set out in the attached schedules, made part of the official minutes. The bulk of the packet's middle sections is the November 2018 check register run by fund, together with listings of ACH debits, wire transfers and P-Card purchases.

**Personnel.** Item 9.A is a consideration of elementary and secondary personnel recommendations.

**Business 11.A: Boulan and Larson locker replacement.** The resolution awards the bid for locker replacement at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools in the amount of $152,065.00.

**Business 11.B: 2019 roof replacement project.** The resolution awards the roof replacement bid as set out in the attached schedule, as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The schedule covers elementary schools, Smith Middle School and the Operations Building, and names Quality Roofing for Athens High School at $197,421.00, with a contingency of $78,212.10, for a total of $860,333.10.

**Business 11.C: Troy High School pool renovation.** The resolution awards the pool renovation as set out in the attached schedule, as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the Sinking Fund: B & B Pools for pool upgrades at $209,090.00, Shoreview Electric for electrical work at $123,400.00, Paint Plus for painting at $149,300.00, and a contingency of $48,179.00, for a total of $529,969.00.

**Business 11.D: 2019 flooring replacement program.** The resolution awards flooring replacement work as set out in the attached schedule, as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund: Conventional Carpet, Inc. at $829,598.03, Kuhn Specialty Flooring at $112,500.00, additional and emergency flooring at $15,000.00, and a contingency of $11,250.00, for a total of $968,348.03.

**Business 11.E: Early Childhood Center signage.** The resolution awards the bid for signage for the Early Childhood Center to ASI Sign in the amount of $30,827.94.

Taken together the five business items commit well over two million dollars of capital work in a single January meeting — the flooring and roofing programs alone account for $968,348.03 and $860,333.10 — drawn across the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, the Building Site and Sinking Fund and the Early Childhood Center accounts, and set against a backdrop in which the district was simultaneously completing the new preschool and preparing the third series of its 2013 bond.

**Other.** Item 13.A adopts the 2019 Board committee assignments. Item 13.B is a first reading of revisions to board policies, which return for second reading and adoption at the following meeting.
